newsitem.title: USA: Suiza to buy dairy companies for $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Suiza to buy dairy companies for $400 mln.

text.p: Suiza Foods Corp said Monday it signed a definitive agreement to buy Dairy Fresh LP, Garelick Farms and several other dairy and affiliated plastic companies for about $400 million in cash and stock.

Dairy Fresh, a milk and ice cream processor based in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, reported sales of about $125 million in its 1996 fiscal year. The other combined businesses had annual sales of about $370 million in their most recent fiscal years.
Beside Garelick Farms in Franklin, Massachusetts, the other acquired operations include: Fairdale Farms in Bennington, Vermont and Grant's Dairy in Bangor, Maine.

They also include the Miscoe Springs water bottling company in Mendon, Massachusetts and 16 plastic bottle manufacturing operations located in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia.
Suiza said it expects to complete the deal within 60 days pending regulatory approval. It expects to complete the Dairy Fresh deal by July 1.
Financing for these deals will be provided under a recently expanded $700 million senior lending facility underwritten by First Union National Bank and First National Bank of Chicago.
The company said it expects the Garelick Farm deal will be immediately accretive to earnings and will improve efficiency and profitability.
